statements.text: County and district courts share original jurisdiction in covered civil actions where the debt, damages or value of claimed personal property is $25,000 or less. The county court also has jurisdiction of counterclaims in those actions when the counterclaim does not exceed $25,000.

In money-judgment actions commenced in a court of record of appropriate limited jurisdiction, the 2024 statute sets docket fees for each plaintiff, petitioner, third-party plaintiff and party filing a cross claim or counterclaim. The fee is $85 for less than $1,000, $105 for $1,000 to less than $15,000, and $135 for $15,000 through $25,000. The statutory exceptions in subsections (1)(c)(IV) and (1)(c)(V) are for the small claims division docket fees and fees for filing an answer to a forcible entry and detainer complaint. A defendant or third-party defendant is charged no fee for filing an answer to a forcible entry and detainer complaint, regardless of whether the answer includes a counterclaim or cross claim.
A county civil complaint is filed with the clerk in the county of venue. Local filing arrangements govern electronic filing availability under C.R.C.P. 121 § 1-26.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 121, § 1-26

statements.text: Service of process in county civil court is due within 63 days after the complaint is filed. The C.R.C.P. 300 series governs the deadlines for service and proof of service.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 300 series

statements.text: County and district courts share original jurisdiction in actions to foreclose liens under article 20 of title 38 and in cases of forcible entry, forcible detainer or unlawful detainer, except when such cases involve the boundary or title to real property and except as provided in § 13-40-109. In these subsection (2) cases the county court judgment for rent, damages on account of unlawful detention, damages for injury to property and damages incurred under article 20 of title 38 cannot exceed a total of $25,000, exclusive of costs and attorney fees. In these cases, on and after January 1, 2019, the county court lacks jurisdiction if the monthly rental value of the property exceeds $25,000.
C.R.S. § 13-32-101(1)(c)(III.5) governs the current county civil docket fees.
County civil actions permit the full range of discovery under the C.R.C.P. 300 series.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 300 series

statements.text: A party may appeal a county court civil judgment to district court by filing a notice of appeal in the county court and an appeal bond with the county court clerk within fourteen days after entry of judgment. If a motion for new trial is made within fourteen days, the time for appeal is extended until fourteen days after disposition of that motion and only matters raised on the motion are considered. The appellant's brief is filed within twenty-one days after the record is filed in district court and a copy is served on the appellee. The appellee may file an answering brief within twenty-one days after service. The time for filing briefs and answers may be extended at the district court's discretion. Unless there is further review by the supreme court upon writ of certiorari, the district court judgment on appeal is certified to the county court for action as directed by the district court. In a trial de novo or when the judgment is modified, the judgment is that of the district court and is enforced therefrom.
The C.R.C.P. 300 series governs when a county civil appeal proceeds by trial de novo in district court.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 300 series
